A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Multilingual Routing in Mixture-of-Experts. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing analyses across four MoE models and intervention experiments on MGSM and the medical subset of Global-MMLU.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and provides additional reporting of identified experts in Appendix A.8.

M1.justification: Expert identification, threshold selection, soft logit steering and hard activation/deactivation remain unchanged, including Equations 3–5. The added explanation of how interventions preserve routing diversity does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FLORES/Belebele language coverage, GSM8K-Instruct and MedInstruct identification data, and MGSM and Global-MMLU medical evaluations. Appendix A.8 introduces no new dataset, task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The same unmodified models and intervention controls are compared. The deactivation and random-layer comparisons remain in Section 5.4; newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains the same models, target layers, thresholds and intervention strengths. MGSM remains a 250-sample, two-shot exact-match evaluation, and the medical evaluation remains 420 samples with zero-shot accuracy.

E4.justification: The deactivation, layer-sensitivity and expert-overlap analyses are retained. Appendix A.8 provides maps of the expert-identification analysis already described across all four models in v1, rather than a distinct new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statistical-significance assertions without adding run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-test details. The 500 token-pair sampling procedure is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure A.11 newly reports the GPT-OSS expert locations and explicit counts of nine math and 63 multilingual experts with zero overlap; v1 already stated the general zero-overlap finding. Section 4.3 removes the Farsi–Arabic low-divergence example. All benchmark values in Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–8, including entropy normalization and intervention formulas, are unchanged. No theorem, proof or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and six numbered findings retain the same core claims about routing alignment, expert specialization and multilingual improvements from steering. The expanded conclusion emphasizes findings already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets expert separation through the dissociation of language and thought. Sections 5.3–6 add explanations about preserved routing diversity, excessive steering disrupting aggregation weights, and interventions outside the middle layers disrupting meaningful specialization.

D1.justification: v2 removes the Section 4.3 footnote explaining that cross-domain divergence is computed after averaging expert importance across sequences because samples cannot be paired. This reduces procedural documentation without establishing a changed experiment; checkpoint, library and intervention details otherwise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kargaran et al. on multilingual alignment, Mahowald et al. on language–thought dissociation, and Xue et al. on OpenMoE routing. Other changes, including Fayyaz et al. changing from 2025 to 2026, update publication information for existing references.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, expands explanatory paragraphs and the conclusion, moves the hyperparameter discussion into Section 6, and adds Appendix A.8. The overall section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix A.8 adds two expert-location maps, with Figure A.10 explicitly providing another view of Figure 5. Figures A.5–A.8 receive informative captions replacing placeholders, and some figures and tables are resized or relocated. Existing plot images are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through corrected appendix captions, explicit expert-location maps and fuller explanations of intervention sensitivity. These gains are partly offset by deleting the cross-domain aggregation footnote. The main experimental evidence and statistical reporting remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
